articles.title_orig: Woman’s body recovered after medevac helicopter crash off Catalina Island
articles.title_zh: Woman’s body recovered after medevac helicopter crash off Catalina Island
articles.content_orig:
AVALON, Calif. (KABC) -- The Los Angeles County Fire Department says that the missing person in a helicopter crash off Catalina Island that killed a pilot and nurse has been found.
The agency said they located the person shortly before 6:30 p.m. Thursday and is in the "custody" of the L.A. County Sheriff's Department. A dive team remains at the scene.
No further details were immediately known.
This comes as family members identified the missing person as a longtime housekeeper living on the island.
The aircraft was carrying five people when it went down in the water off of Pebbly Beach around 7:50 p.m. Wednesday soon after takeoff, according to the U.S. Coast Guard. Initial reports indicated that there were only three people on the aircraft.
"We have three people calling for help," a first responder is heard saying in an audio recording of an emergency broadcast. "We do have survivors in the water."
The L.A. County Fire Department later confirmed that two people died, two were hospitalized and a fifth person remained missing.
Family members identified that fifth person as Catalina Romero. They told Eyewitness News that she lived and worked as a housekeeper on Catalina Island for over 20 years and was the mother of three boys.
Relatives and friends said that Romero took her lunch break during her work shift and became ill. They told Eyewitness News that she had an allergic reaction to something she ate and was taken to the emergency room on the island. That's when they decided to send her over to the mainland.
L.A. County Sheriff Robert Luna confirmed at a news conference Thursday afternoon that the missing person was a patient being transported to the mainland for treatment.
"She's my aunt. Right now we're waiting to recover her body and eventually get some closure for the whole entire family right now," said Maria Tamayo. "She was just a loving and caring mother."
Relatives also said Romero's 20-year-old son went with her in the medical helicopter to help translate.
Sheriff Luna said that they are not identifying victims by name at this time, but described the two people that died as the male pilot and a female nurse. He also said another medic and a fourth person, a man, were taken to the same hospital where they are being treated.
AIR7 flew over Ronald Reagan UCLA Medical Center where at least one of the victims was seen being wheeled off a helicopter.
"Two of those people were last reported (as being) in stable condition, at a higher level of care," Cpt. Stacey Crecy of the U.S. Coast Guard, speaking to reporters at an early morning news conference, said of the survivors.
A memorial service was held Thursday on Catalina Island near the crash site to mourn and pray for those involved in the crash.
Search operations continued through the night for the missing person.
Capt. Crecy told reporters at Thursday's news conference that the search has covered over 130 sq. nautical miles so far, with approximately 20 hours of continuous searching for the missing person, and they've had ideal search conditions throughout.
Search and rescue boats were seen on the water early Thursday afternoon. Crecy said teams will be extending their search.
Hours after the crash, REACH Air Medical Services confirmed that one of their helicopters was involved in the incident.
"We are aware of an incident involving a REACH Air Medical Services helicopter. At this time, we are gathering information and coordinating with emergency responders and authorities. We are unable to provide additional details at this stage and will share more information when it becomes available. Our immediate concern is for the well-being of those involved.," said a spokesperson for the company.
The L.A. County Fire on-scene lifeguard dive rescue team located the helicopter wreckage under 218 feet of water using a remotely-operated vehicle, L.A. County Fire Chief Anthony Marrone said at Thursday's news conference -- adding that rescue boats arrived within three minutes of them receiving the emergency call.
Sheriff Robert Luna said that sheriff's personnel assisted with the recovery and preservation of debris for federal investigators.
The National Transportation Safety Board and Federal Aviation Administration are investigating the crash.
